newsitem.title: USA: Beneficial rain likely for dry Kansas wheat areas.
newsitem.headline: Beneficial rain likely for dry Kansas wheat areas.

text.p: Beneficial rain was likely in western Kansas, where the hard red winter wheat badly needs moisture to fully develop ahead of harvest next month, crop sources and meteorologists said.
"We do have some chance for showers over the course of the next five days," said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist.
Rainfall from Wednesday to the weekend may total 0.25 to 0.75 inch, which may nourish wheat that has had less than 30 percent of its normal May moisture, said Burgio.
Goodland, in northwest Kansas, has had 0.37 inch of rain so far this month or 17 percent of normal. Dodge City in southwest Kansas has had 0.55 inch, or 28 percent of normal.
Kansas soil moisture declined during the week ended Sunday and wheat in the dryest areas needed moisture, said the latest weekly state agricultural statistics service crop report.
It rated Kansas wheat 11 percent excellent, 44 percent good, 30 fair, 11 poor and four percent very poor.
Normal to below normal temperatures should be common over much of the hard red winter wheat belt through this week, meteorologists said.
Freeze-Notis Weather forecasted this week's rain may total 0.50 to 1.50 inches in the dry western Kansas wheat areas.
"We look for beneficial rains falling in the driest areas and could last from late Tuesday to late Friday," said Craig Solberg, Freese-Notis meteorologist.

Solberg said the same low pressure system that kept the Midwest abnormally cool this spring, prevented moist air from the south from moving north into western and northern Kansas. That low pressure system was still in place, but appears to have weakened slightly.
